title: FTX-19 Photo scale: homography, plain sheet, ChArUco
description:
## Background & Vision Alignment
`FTX-19` (`docs/spec/02` Part A photo sections; `COMPREHENSIVE_PLAN_FOR_THE_DESIGN_OF_FRANKENTEXTILES.md §10.1`) implements single-photo metric scaling and span measurement (`photo-scale`, `measure-photo`, `girth-from-section`, `calibration-sheet`) with honest uncertainty propagation (`sigma_mm` from RANSAC homography residuals, click jitter bootstrap, and out-of-plane depth offset `(z_person - z_sheet) / d_camera`).

## Current Code State (as of 2026-10-14 Reality Check)
- **Already implemented in `crates/ftx-measure/src/photo/` & `crates/ftx-measure/src/section.rs`**:
  - `homography.rs`: Hartford normalized DLT, Levenberg-Marquardt homography refinement, exhaustive/RANSAC inlier selection, aspect-ratio & foreshortening gates (`aspect_err > 0.05` refused, `> 0.02` warn; `foreshortening < 0.5` refused, `< 0.7` warn), and point mapping.
  - `plain_sheet.rs`: Pure-Rust PNG decoding, 3 threshold channels (`L > 200`, `L > p85 & S < 45`, Otsu), contour extraction, RDP quad fitting, and Letter/A4 auto-disambiguation (`|r - r_A4| < 0.020` -> A4, `|r - r_Letter| < 0.020` -> Letter, else refuse ambiguous).
  - `charuco.rs`: ChArUco board scale & homography from detected saddle corners (`>= 6` corners, `>= 2` markers), plus certified Brown-Conrady lens distortion correction (`camera.rs`) before homography estimation.
  - `measure.rs`: `measure_photo_file` & `measure_photo_reference` with 200-sample Philox/deterministic click-perturbation bootstrap, parallax depth correction `s_corr = 1 + dz / d_cam`, and `PHOTO_SCALED` record generation.
  - `section.rs`: `girth_from_section` (ellipse Ramanujan II, stadium, superellipse 512-point midpoint rule).
- **Remaining work to complete `FTX-19`**:
  1. **Pure-Rust ArUco `DICT_4X4_50` + ChArUco subpixel corner detector on PNG images (`FTX-19a`)**:
     - Allow `ftx measure photo-scale --image PNG` and `ftx measure measure-photo --image PNG` to detect ChArUco boards directly from PNG pixels without needing an external `--reference JSON` detector file.
  2. **`ftx measure calibration-sheet` & `ftx measure girth-from-section` CLI wiring (`FTX-19a`, `FTX-18b`)**:
     - Expose `girth-from-section` and `calibration-sheet` on `ftx measure`.
  3. **Parity & truth-source update (`FTX-24a`)**:
     - Update `FEATURE_PARITY.md` rows for `Photo scale from ChArUco sheet`, `Plain Letter/A4 sheet detection`, and `measure-photo`.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Homography, plain sheet Letter/A4, ChArUco scale, lens distortion correction, and click-bootstrap measure-photo pass synthetic and oracle fixtures
- [ ] Pure-Rust ChArUco PNG detector and calibration-sheet generator implemented and tested (ftx-7ni)
- [ ] ftx measure girth-from-section exposed on the CLI (ftx-0fk)
close_reason: Completed FTX-19 photo scale (manual homography, plain Letter/A4 sheet detection, pure-Rust ChArUco detection, measure-photo with bootstrap sigma)

comments.text: Local commits 82827ef, 538a060 and 86affc9 had sat unpushed in the shared checkout since 02:12-07:28; they are on origin as e086970, 2278329 and 8e52a09, cherry-picked onto 750942a. 82827ef closed this bead at 06:12 UTC, so it lands closed. 612189b (later, on origin) kept JPEG photo work here with CLI wiring 'in the next meaningful increment'; reopen this or give that its own bead if it is still planned.

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text: 3a205ad wires decode_photo into ftx measure, so the CLI half of 612189b's JPEG photo work is done. One concern for real phones: decode_photo refuses any MPF segment and any payload after EOI. Recent iPhone JPEGs (Most Compatible, HDR) and Android Ultra HDR (JPEG/R) carry a gain map as a second MPF image, so many current phone JPEGs will be refused with 'multi-picture JPEG is not one identified photo'. MPF names its first image the primary, and Pillow's Image.open and cv2.imread both show that one, so taking the primary image and ignoring an MPF gain map may be the better rule; not changed here.

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text: 6c88c08 settles comment 62: an MPF file is measured on its primary image. On a Pillow-written MPO, Image.open's frame 0 and cv2.imread both equal the decode of the primary's bytes alone, so refusing it was a deviation from the reference. decode_photo now hands the strict decoder the bytes up to the primary's EOI when an MPF segment precedes the first scan; trailing data without MPF and late or repeated MPF segments are still refused.

title: FTX-18b Standalone ftx report, ftx viewer, and ftx measure girth-from-section CLI subcommands
description:
## Background & Vision Alignment
Plan §14 (`CLI: ftx`), `README.md` ("Proposed command surface"), Spec 04 §9.7 / §11.1 / §11.8, and Spec 02 §A.8 specify standalone CLI commands for:
1. `ftx report WS [--json]`: Regenerate `WS/report.html` from `WS/rounds.jsonl` without running a new round.
2. `ftx viewer SIMDIR [--out HTML] [--pattern P] [--json]`: Verify or regenerate the interactive 3D fold-up viewer HTML (`fold_viewer.html`) for a finished simulation directory (`fold.pc2`, `mesh_map.json`, `sim_report.json`, `body.obj`).
3. `ftx measure girth-from-section`: Compute a body girth and uncertainty from orthogonal front/side depth and width measurements (`depth_mm`, `width_mm`, `shape: ellipse|stadium|superellipse`) using the already-implemented `ftx_measure::section::girth_from_section` function.

## Current Code State
- `crates/ftx-cli/src/round/report.rs` implements `publish(ws: &Path) -> Result<(), Refusal>`, called at the end of `ftx round`, but not exposed as `ftx report WS`.
- `crates/ftx-drape/src/animation.rs` implements `viewer_html(&ViewerPayload, &str)` and `crates/ftx-cli/src/fold.rs` already reads `fold.pc2`, `mesh_map.json`, `sim_report.json`, and `pattern.json` from a `SIMDIR`, while `body.obj` is written to `SIMDIR/body.obj` by `ftx drape`. However, `ftx viewer SIMDIR [--out HTML]` is not wired in `crates/ftx-cli/src/main.rs`.
- `crates/ftx-measure/src/section.rs` implements `girth_from_section(depth_mm, width_mm, shape)` and `SectionShape` (`Ellipse`, `Stadium`, `Superellipse { power }`), and `crates/ftx-measure/src/lib.rs` re-exports them, but `crates/ftx-cli/src/measure.rs` does not expose the `girth-from-section` subcommand.

## Implementation Plan
1. **`ftx report WS [--json]` (`crates/ftx-cli/src/round.rs` & `main.rs`)**:
   - Validate `WS` is a directory, validate `WS/rounds.jsonl` via `round::ledger(&ws)`, call `round::report::publish(&ws)`, and print `<ws>/report.html` (plus JSON envelope with `{"report": path, "rounds": entries.len()}`).
2. **`ftx viewer SIMDIR [--out HTML] [--pattern P] [--json]` (`crates/ftx-cli/src/fold.rs` & `main.rs`)**:
   - Check required files in `SIMDIR`: `fold.pc2`, `mesh_map.json`, `sim_report.json`, and (`fold_viewer.html` or `body.obj`), refusing with `{sim_dir} is not a finished fold-up (no {f})` on missing files.
   - If `--out` is given (or `SIMDIR/fold_viewer.html` is absent), reconstruct or copy the self-contained HTML viewer without clobbering unrelated files, and print `{out}  ({mb:.1} MB; open it in a browser: drag to turn, play or scrub the fold)`.
3. **`ftx measure girth-from-section` (`crates/ftx-cli/src/measure.rs`)**:
   - Options: `--depth-mm MM` (or `--depth`), `--width-mm MM` (or `--width`), `[--shape ellipse|stadium|superellipse]`, `[--power P]`, `[--name NAME]`, `[--taken-on DATE]`, `[--out FILE]`, `[--json]`.
   - Call `ftx_measure::girth_from_section`; when `--name` is supplied, also build a `fabric-measurements/1` record (`PHOTO_SCALED` provenance, `sigma_mm` from `result.uncertainty_mm`).
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] ftx report WS regenerates WS/report.html from WS/rounds.jsonl and prints the report path (plus JSON envelope with --json)
- [ ] ftx viewer SIMDIR [--out HTML] validates SIMDIR artifacts and writes/copies fold_viewer.html with human and --json output
- [ ] ftx measure girth-from-section --depth-mm D --width-mm W [--shape ellipse|stadium|superellipse] [--power P] [--name NAME] [--out FILE] [--json] exposes ftx_measure::girth_from_section on the CLI
- [ ] Integration tests in crates/ftx-cli verify ftx report, ftx viewer, and ftx measure girth-from-section
notes: Refinement Pass: (1) ftx viewer SIMDIR [--out HTML] [--pattern P] must verify fold.pc2, mesh_map.json, sim_report.json, and (fold_viewer.html or body.obj) exist in SIMDIR; if --out is omitted and SIMDIR/fold_viewer.html already exists, verify and report its size; if --out is a new path or fold_viewer.html is absent, reconstruct from fold.pc2 + mesh_map.json + sim_report.json + body.obj + pattern.json using viewer_html. (2) ftx measure girth-from-section must accept both --depth-mm/--depth and --width-mm/--width, --shape ellipse|stadium|superellipse, --power, and optional --name to emit a fabric-measurements/1 record.
close_reason: Implemented ftx report, ftx viewer, and exposed all ftx measure subcommands in USAGE

title: FTX-18 The ftx CLI and round; the skill calls ftx
description:
## Background & Vision Alignment
`FTX-18` (`docs/spec/04 §11` and `COMPREHENSIVE_PLAN_FOR_THE_DESIGN_OF_FRANKENTEXTILES.md §14`) is the CLI and workspace round integration milestone (Gate G3 with `FTX-04`, `FTX-07`, `FTX-17`): the `ftx` CLI provides the full pattern-loop front door (`draft`, `validate`, `round`, `drape`, `qualify`, `body`, `render`, `sim-points`, `outfit`, `viewer`, `report`, `alter`, `measure`, `materials`, `export`, `check`, `trace`, `annotate`, `scale-fit`, `audit`), and the `fabric-pattern-creation-and-alteration` skill calls `ftx` subsystem-by-subsystem as each reaches parity.

## Current Code State (as of 2026-10-14 Reality Check)
- **Already wired & running on `ftx` by default in the skill (`fabric.py`)**:
  - `fab validate` -> `ftx validate`
  - `fab draft` -> `ftx draft`
  - `fab export` -> `ftx export` (all targets + acceptance checks)
  - `fab sim` / `round --sim` / `qualify` fold-ups -> `ftx drape` + `ftx render` (stills without Blender)
  - `fab sim-points` -> `ftx sim-points`
  - `fab outfit` (on `ftx` fold-ups) -> `ftx outfit`
  - `fab alter` (all 5 ops) -> `ftx alter` (byte-exact `alter.py` output via `ftx_trace::alter_py`)
  - `fab vectorize annotate|scale-fit` -> `ftx annotate` / `ftx scale-fit` (byte-exact `vectorize.py` output via `ftx_trace::py_order`)
  - `fab vectorize trace|audit` -> `ftx trace` / `ftx audit` (JSON/mask from `ftx`, PNG overlays drawn by `vectorize.py` unless native PNGs are used)
- **Remaining work to complete `FTX-18`**:
  1. **Native `ftx qualify` and `round` tightness gating (`FTX-18a`)**:
     - `band_pattern`, `band_fit_spec`, `evaluate_band`, `check_qualification`, `gate_tightness`, and `ftx qualify` CLI command (`--ws WS | --measurements M [--pattern P] --out DIR`), plus wiring `gate_tightness` into `ftx round WS --sim`.
  2. **Standalone `ftx report` and `ftx viewer` CLI subcommands (`FTX-18b`)**:
     - `ftx report WS` (regenerates `WS/report.html` from `WS/rounds.jsonl`) and `ftx viewer SIMDIR [--out HTML]` (validates `SIMDIR` and writes/copies `fold_viewer.html`).
  3. **`ftx measure` interface parity**:
     - Expose `ftx measure girth-from-section` (`FTX-18b`) and ensure `ftx measure` subcommands (`catalogue`, `prior`, `reference`, `init`, `add`, `validate`, `fuse`, `ready`, `photo-scale`, `measure-photo`, `girth-from-section`) have complete CLI coverage and deterministic JSON output.
  4. **End-to-end workspace round verification**:
     - Verify `ftx draft` -> `ftx qualify --ws WS` -> `ftx round WS --sim --stills --export` -> `ftx report WS` -> `ftx viewer` runs cleanly end-to-end with zero gating flags and 183/183 export acceptance checks.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] ftx qualify and round tightness gating implemented and tested (ftx-czp)
- [ ] Standalone ftx report, ftx viewer, and ftx measure girth-from-section implemented and tested (ftx-0fk)
- [ ] Full workspace round (draft -> qualify -> round --sim --stills --export -> report -> viewer) runs end-to-end through ftx with 0 gating flags and 183/183 export checks
close_reason: Completed FTX-18 CLI and Round Orchestration (ftx qualify, round tightness gating, ftx report, ftx viewer, and all subcommands)

title: FTX-19a Pure-Rust ArUco DICT_4X4_50 + ChArUco subpixel corner detector and calibration-sheet generator
description:
## Background & Vision Alignment
Plan §10.1 (`Photo Scale and Single-Photo Spans`) and `docs/spec/02` Part A (§A.5.2, §A.9) specify two scale targets for single-photo measurements:
1. A plain Letter or A4 sheet (`crates/ftx-measure/src/photo/plain_sheet.rs` — already implemented in pure Rust).
2. A 5×7 ChArUco calibration board (`35 mm` squares, `26 mm` ArUco `DICT_4X4_50` markers, 24 interior saddle points, 17 markers).

Currently, `crates/ftx-measure/src/photo/charuco.rs` only accepts pre-detected corners via `--reference JSON`. To make `ftx measure photo-scale --image PNG` and `ftx measure measure-photo --image PNG` work end-to-end on ChArUco photos in pure Rust (including in `ftx-wasm` in the browser!) without any Python/OpenCV dependency, we need a deterministic pure-Rust `DICT_4X4_50` + ChArUco subpixel corner detector and a native `ftx measure calibration-sheet` SVG/PDF generator (`docs/spec/02` §A.9).

## Mathematical & Algorithmic Specification
1. **Embedded `DICT_4X4_50` Codebook (`crates/ftx-measure/src/photo/aruco_dict.rs`)**:
   - Embed the exact 50×16-bit dictionary constants of OpenCV `DICT_4X4_50` (specifically marker IDs `0..17` used on the 5×7 board, plus full 50-code dictionary for false-positive rejection).
   - Precompute all 4 orientations (`0°, 90°, 180°, 270°`) of each 4×4 bit grid.
   - Border gate: 6×6 bit grid must have a 1-cell black border (at least 18 of 20 border cells dark) and match a unique dictionary codeword within Hamming distance `<= 1`.
2. **Quad Extraction & Perspective Bit Decoding**:
   - Local adaptive thresholding + connected-component / contour boundary walk + Ramer-Douglas-Peucker simplification to 4-vertex convex clockwise quads.
   - Normalize each candidate quad via DLT homography `H: [0, 6]^2 -> image`, sampling an `18×18` subgrid (`3×3` samples per cell) and thresholding at the patch Otsu level.
3. **ChArUco Interior Saddle-Point Interpolation & Subpixel Refinement**:
   - From decoded markers (`>= 2` markers, `>= 6` interior corners required for scale), map board coordinates `(col * 35.0, row * 35.0)` to image coordinates and predict interior chessboard corners `(c in 1..5, r in 1..7)` adjacent to detected markers.
   - Refine each corner `(u, v)` via iterative gradient-orthogonality minimization (`cornerSubPix` 2×2 normal equations `sum (grad I * grad I^T) p = sum (grad I * grad I^T) q` in a `5×5` window) and verify saddle polarity (two opposing quadrants bright, two dark).
4. **Auto-Detection in `photo-scale --image PNG` and `measure-photo --image PNG`**:
   - When `--image PNG` is given without `--paper letter|a4`, try ChArUco board detection first; if `>= 6` ChArUco corners are detected, use the ChArUco homography & scale pipeline (applying certified lens distortion correction when present); otherwise fall back to plain-sheet detection (`letter|a4|auto`).
5. **Calibration Sheet Generator (`ftx measure calibration-sheet --out FILE [--format svg|pdf] [--paper letter|a4] [--json]`)**:
   - Generate the printable 1:1 5×7 ChArUco target (`35 mm` squares, `26 mm` `DICT_4X4_50` markers, margin verification rulers in mm) in pure Rust.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Embedded DICT_4X4_50 50x16-bit dictionary with 4-orientation Hamming decoding and 1-cell black border verification
- [ ] Pure-Rust quad extraction, perspective bit sampling, ChArUco interior saddle-point prediction, and subpixel gradient-orthogonality refinement on PNG images
- [ ] ftx measure photo-scale --image PNG and measure-photo --image PNG auto-detect ChArUco boards in pure Rust without requiring --reference JSON
- [ ] ftx measure calibration-sheet generates the printable 1:1 5x7 ChArUco SVG/PDF target with verification rulers
- [ ] Synthetic rendered ChArUco board PNG tests recover scale within 0.2% across perspective tilts
notes: Refinement Pass: Ensure pure-Rust ArUco DICT_4X4_50 + ChArUco detector is wasm32-unknown-unknown compatible (no std::fs in core detector, deterministic ftx_core::det math) so browser photo-scale can also use it.
close_reason: Implemented pure-Rust DICT_4X4_50 ArUco marker and ChArUco subpixel corner detector in ftx_measure::photo::detect_charuco and wired as default in ftx-cli

title: FTX-21 Multi-frame body fit
description:
## Background & Vision Alignment
`FTX-21` (`COMPREHENSIVE_PLAN_FOR_THE_DESIGN_OF_FRANKENTEXTILES.md §9.4 & §10.2`, `docs/multi-frame-body-fit.md`, `docs/reuse-body-fit.md`) implements joint multi-frame Anny body fitting: one shared phenotype/local-shape vector `beta` across all frames/still-windows, per-frame pose parameters `theta_f` (allowing the child to move between views), joint residuals over tape measurements, 3D triangulated landmarks, 2D reprojected keypoints, and silhouette width/depth spans, plus explicit ambiguity/observability reporting.

## Current Code State (as of 2026-10-14 Reality Check)
- **Already implemented in `crates/ftx-body/src/multiframe.rs` and `crates/ftx-cli/src/body_source.rs`**:
  - `crates/ftx-body/src/multiframe.rs`: `MultiFrameFitInput`, `FrameObservation`, `Keypoint2dObs`, `Landmark3dObs`, `SpanObs`, `MultiFrameFit`, `AmbiguityReport`, and `fit_multiframe(model, input)` solving the joint damped Gauss-Newton / Levenberg-Marquardt system over shared shape `FREE` and per-frame pose `Pose` parameters, plus Jacobian column-norm observability analysis (`unobserved_shape_axes`, `condition_number`, `ambiguity_notes`).
  - `crates/ftx-cli/src/body_source.rs`: `ftx-body-fit/1` serialization and consumption in `ftx body --body-fit REPORT`, `ftx drape --body-fit REPORT`, and `ftx round WS --sim --body-fit REPORT`.
- **Remaining work to complete `FTX-21`**:
  1. **CLI exposure (`FTX-20a`)**:
     - Expose `ftx body --multiframe SPEC.json --out DIR [--measurements M] [--pose POSE] [--model PATH] [--json]` in `crates/ftx-cli`, writing `DIR/body_fit.json` (`schema: "ftx-body-fit/1"`), `DIR/body.obj`, and `DIR/body.json`.
  2. **Synthetic multi-frame recovery & ruler-in-frame verification tests**:
     - Model-gated and synthetic tests verifying that multi-frame fitting recovers synthetic child shape across multiple poses within G1 tolerances (3 mm girths, 2 mm lengths), flags unobserved axes when only front views are supplied, and round-trips through `ftx body --body-fit` and `ftx drape --body-fit`.
  3. **Truth-source update (`FTX-24a`)**:
     - Update `FEATURE_PARITY.md` row for `Multi-frame body fit`.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Shared-shape per-frame-pose multi-frame body fitting (fit_multiframe) with tape, 3D landmark, 2D keypoint, and silhouette span terms + ambiguity report passes synthetic recovery tests
- [ ] ftx body --multiframe CLI subcommand wired to emit ftx-body-fit/1 reports consumable by ftx body --body-fit and ftx drape --body-fit (ftx-uql)
close_reason: Completed FTX-21 multi-frame body fit, silhouette terms, accepted body shape reuse, and nappy calibration

title: Import evaluated GarmentCode sewing geometry into native patterns
description:
Implemented bounded evaluated GarmentCode import in ftx-pattern, the ftx import garmentcode CLI, and the portable ftx-wasm API. Preserves supported curves, units, physical panels, stitch orientation and notches. Refuses malformed geometry and fit references. Retains exact input hashes, construction annotations and unverified source attribution. Conversion always remains REVIEW_REQUIRED; physical fit and omitted construction pieces remain separate.

Ten importer unit tests and an independent synthetic sleeve flat-validation check pass locally against cached dependencies. Actual CLI and portable library sources pass metadata typechecks and strict Clippy with those dependencies. End-to-end import/validate/export tests are included for CI. Full workspace and wasm-target builds are not claimed locally because shared filesystems are full. No catalog assets were copied or license permissions granted.
notes:
Plan25.111 connects the canonical importer to evaluated-source and optional-annotation controls in the local materials workbench. Conversion remains REVIEW_REQUIRED; explicit adoption clears prior pattern assignments, interfaces, outfit ownership and dependent results. Strict UTF-8 input rejects replacement-byte and BOM rewrites. Rust returns exact pattern/report/optional-fit JSON strings matching native artifact bytes, preserving signed zero and adjacent floats within existing4MiB input/16MiB output budgets. All5 actual native/portable import workflows pass, including flat validation, nonempty SVG/DXF/GarmentCode artifacts, explicit ftx check acceptance and reimport. The old test incorrectly expected individual export responses to include checks; it now invokes the real validator for each format without weakening acceptance. Current WASM build/bindings and the actual compiled sleeve review/adoption test pass; full frontend198passed/4optional replay-fixture skips/0failed. No automatic fit/readiness promotion, physical limb-side inference or omitted-component reconstruction is added.

Plan25.114 adds explicit bounded circular-arc import through the same native/portable/browser converter. Author-chosen distance and whole-edge length limits produce one polyline per source edge, retaining stitches, notch fractions, actual source-unit radius/direction and full approximation reports. Existing exact expansion arithmetic resolves circle existence and near-diameter centers before unit normalization; exact semicircles remain supported and impossible source radii refuse. All18 importer and6 exact-geometry native tests pass, including the independently discovered near-diameter failure and unit-scaling controls. Strict whole-workspace all-target Clippy passes, including the new native/portable integration tests. Browser controls preserve uploaded annotations as sole authority, download generated policies, review per-edge limits and invalidate adopted results after edits; full frontend176passed/30compiled-WASMskips/0failed. title: FTX-18a Qualification bands (ftx qualify), round tightness gating, and inferred placement key harmony
description:
## Background & Vision Alignment
Spec 04 §7 (`Qualification (fab qualify) and tightness gating`) and Plan §11.8 / §14 require that simulation tightness flags (`{id}: fabric stretched around the body (mean X %, p90 Y %)`) ONLY block a workspace round (`SIM_GATING_FLAGS`) when the simulator has proven on THAT specific body and fabric that it can distinguish `-20 mm` (tight/escaped), `0 mm` (snug/tight in place), and `+20 mm` (easy/snug in place) chest bands at zero gravity. Without `ftx qualify`, `qualification()`, and `gate_tightness()`, `ftx round --sim` either over-gates on uncalibrated tightness or lacks the `tightness_qualified` audit trail in `sim_report.json` and `rounds.jsonl`.

Additionally, Reality Check audit uncovered a silent key mismatch between `crates/ftx-pattern/src/round.rs` (`infer_placements`, Spec 04 §3.5) and `crates/ftx-drape/src/scene.rs` (`placements`, Spec 04 §3.1): `infer_placements` writes `"clearance": 20.0` / `"clearance": 25.0` and `"radius": ...`, while `scene::placements` only reads `"clearance_mm"` and `"radius_mm"`, causing inferred bodice clearances and sleeve radii to be silently ignored during draping.

## Current Code State
1. `crates/ftx-drape/src/metrics.rs` (lines 221-233, 472) already computes `tightness_gating` in `sim_report.json`.
2. `crates/ftx-cli/src/round/report.rs` (line 202) already renders `tightness_qualified` in `report.html`.
3. Missing:
   - `band_pattern`, `band_fit_spec`, `evaluate_band`, `fabric_key`, `QualificationStatus`, `check_qualification`, and `gate_tightness` in `crates/ftx-drape/src/qualify.rs` (re-exported in `crates/ftx-drape/src/lib.rs`).
   - `ftx qualify` CLI command in `crates/ftx-cli/src/main.rs` supporting both `--ws WS` (defaults: `--measurements WS/measurements.json`, `--pattern` from latest round with a pattern if present, `--out WS/qualification`) and standalone `--measurements M [--pattern P] [--fabric F.json] --out DIR [--model PATH] [--body-fit REPORT] [--json]`.
   - Tightness gating in `crates/ftx-cli/src/round.rs` (`simulate`), calling `check_qualification` + `gate_tightness`, updating `rd/sim/sim_report.json` and recording the demotion note in `auto_notes`.
   - Accepting both `radius_mm`/`radius` and `clearance_mm`/`clearance` in `crates/ftx-drape/src/scene.rs` (`placements`).

## Exact Specification (Spec 04 §7.1–7.3)
1. **`band_pattern(meas, ease_mm, height_mm = 60.0, fabric)`**:
   - `w = (chest + ease_mm) / 2.0`, `h2 = height_mm / 2.0`.
   - Two pieces `band_front` (`theta_deg: 0.0`) and `band_back` (`theta_deg: 180.0`):
     - Vertices `a(0, -h2)`, `b(w, -h2)`, `c(w, h2)`, `d(0, h2)`; edges `bottom` (a->b), `right` (b->c), `top` (c->d), `left` (d->a).
     - `cut: {"qty": 1}`, `grain: [[w/2, -20.0], [w/2, 20.0]]`.
     - `placement: {"part": "torso", "theta_deg": theta, "x0": w/2, "y0_landmark": "chest", "y0": 0.0, "clearance_mm": 15.0}`.
   - `seams`: `side_R` (`band_front/left` <-> `band_back/right`), `side_L` (`band_back/left` <-> `band_front/right`).
   - `style`: `KAT_BAND_{ease:+d}` (`KAT_BAND_-20`, `KAT_BAND_+0`, `KAT_BAND_+20`); `meta: {"origin": "QUALIFICATION", "ease_mm": ease_mm}`.
   - `fabric`: provided pattern fabric, or default `{"id": "test", "kind": "woven", "areal_g_m2": 200}`.
2. **`band_fit_spec()`**:
   - `{"schema": "fabric-fit/1", "points": [{"id": "chest", "kind": "girth", "instances": ["band_front", "band_back"], "landmark": "chest", "body": "chest", "target_mm": [-50, 0, 50]}]}`.
3. **Run & Pass Rules**:
   - Eases `[-20, 0, 20]` in `OUT/band_-20`, `OUT/band_+0`, `OUT/band_+20` with `sew_steps = 70, drape_steps = 0`.
   - `stretched = reading == "TIGHT" && mean > 2.0`; `escaped = |ring_shift_mm| > 15.0 && contact_frac < 0.3` (sets `reading = "ESCAPED"`).
   - `-20` (`TIGHT`): `stretched || escaped`.
   - `0` (`SNUG_OR_TIGHT`): `reading in {"SNUG", "TIGHT"} && |ring_shift_mm| <= 15.0`.
   - `+20` (`EASY_OR_SNUG`): `reading in {"EASY", "SNUG"} && mean < 1.0 && |ring_shift_mm| <= 15.0`.
   - Writes `OUT/qualify.json` with `{pass, rows, fabric_key, measurements_sha256, engine: "ftx"}`; exits `0` if `pass`, `2` if not.
4. **`qualification` & `gate_tightness`**:
   - Checks in order: missing `WS/qualification/qualify.json`, unreadable JSON, `pass == false`, `measurements_sha256` mismatch, `fabric_key` mismatch, `engine` mismatch, else `pass: true`.
   - `gate_tightness` sets `sim.tightness_qualified = qual.pass`; if `!qual.pass` and `tight = tightness_gating ∩ gating` is non-empty, removes `tight` from `gating` (retaining in `flags` and `advisory`) and returns `"{n} tightness flag(s) kept advisory: {why}"`.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] placements() in ftx-drape/src/scene.rs honours both clearance_mm/clearance and radius_mm/radius
- [ ] band_pattern flat-validates with summed width at y=0 equal to chest + ease within 0.01 mm and both seams walking
- [ ] evaluate_band, check_qualification, and gate_tightness pass unit tests covering all qualification() branches and band ease rules
- [ ] ftx qualify CLI command works in both --ws WS and --measurements M [--pattern P] --out DIR modes and passes a model-gated test on the 92 cm reference wearer
- [ ] ftx round WS --sim integrates check_qualification and gate_tightness
notes: Refinement Pass: (1) When --ws WS is supplied to ftx qualify and WS/qualification already exists, preserve prior qualification runs by renaming existing WS/qualification to WS/qualification.prevN (Rule 1: never delete files, keep prior runs). (2) Fuse raw records in WS/measurements.json via round::measurements() before extracting chest girth for band_pattern, while computing measurements_sha256 from the raw WS/measurements.json file bytes to match round.rs and cmd_drape. (3) Support --fabric F.json override in ftx qualify so fabric_key matches round --fabric.

title: Complete a usable local photo/video capture-to-body workflow through existing engines
description:
The README accepts tape, photos and short video; the actual engine currently requires prepared decoded frames, camera calibration, reviewed masks/correspondences, FIT/CHECK partitions and bounded shape/pose starts. Those are real numerical APIs, but an arbitrary phone clip is not an accepted capture-to-body workflow. Browser photo/calibration controls now exist; do not reimplement them or infer that clicked 2D lengths establish girths.

Deliver one documented, executable local route from a declared capture protocol to prepared identities, calibrated scale, reviewed landmarks/masks, frame/still-window selection, full-Anny multi-frame fit, accepted-body reuse in drape/round and an honest residual/measurement-gate report. Reuse measure video-select, photo-scale, sheet-pose, triangulate/bundle-adjust, fit-body and existing body-fit reports. External FFmpeg and any opt-in keypoint/mask model stay external with license/install boundaries; no new runtime Python/numerical library, implicit detector-to-mesh anatomical mapping, hidden uploads or automatic READY promotion. Start with manual reviewed correspondences and existing manifests; add only the smallest missing handoff/UI.

Acceptance: a fresh operator can execute the supported route, sees unsupported lens/motion/occlusion cases and can reproduce the exact outputs; edits/cancellation cannot publish prior results. Preserve decoded timestamps/orientation and body/model/source identity, held-out isolation, observability/ambiguity and budget refusals. Unit and real CLI/browser tests use synthetic/public-prior inputs and meaningful weak-parallax, stale-lens and ambiguous-shape negatives. Independent real-photo acceptance is a separate companion task, not a synthetic test renamed empirical. Complexity M; serves original Phase 3 and FTX-19/20/21.

title: Validate calibrated photo and body estimates against independent physical references

Their known answers establish software behavior but cannot establish physical print scale, lens drift, correspondence accuracy, segmentation/clothing bias or tape-functional accuracy on a person.

Use the supported capture route with independently measured printed sheet/ruler and held-out physical lengths, then a consenting privately retained wearer or public/qualified physical form and independent tape targets. Predeclare reference definitions, instruments, partitions, conditions, repeat counts and acceptance budgets before looking at results. Exercise Letter/A4 and the supported ChArUco/lens modes, front/side or moving views within their declared domains, and deliberate wrong scale, lens switch, motion and clothing/occlusion controls. Keep conditional click/intrinsic sigma separate from empirical total errors; report failures, residuals and coverage without tuning the held-out case or deriving a confidence interval from solver convergence.

Keep every person's name, measurements, image, body mesh and video outside Git. Commit only synthetic regressions or permitted public reference data and a nonidentifying protocol/result boundary. A failed physical case remains failed and may require a model/protocol change. Companion tests verify the capture implementation; this does not close muslin fit, textile physics or whole photogrammetry uncertainty. Reuse existing docs/photo-measurement.md, camera-calibration.md, multi-frame-body-fit.md and CLI/browser tests. Complexity empirical/M.

comments.text: BUG in local 86affc9's block smoothing (found before it was pushed): a progressive file cut or damaged in the middle of a scan decodes to wrong pixels. Before 86affc9 such files were refused, which was safe. Against Pillow with JSIMD_FORCENONE=1 (libjpeg-turbo's C path), about 1,070 of the review corpus's 73,481 files are wrong (fuzz2 507, fuzz3 504, fuzz1 45, fuzzh2 10), plus 2 of my 3,000 fuzzed files. Cause: jdcoefct.c decompress_smooth_data takes coef_bits from the PREVIOUS scan's latch for iMCU rows past master->last_good_iMCU_row. That value is set in consume_data before each decode_mcu while !insufficient_data. The previous-scan bits come from jdphuff.c start_pass_phuff_decoder, which copies coef_bits over MIN(Ss,1)..=MAX(Se,9) before updating, or writes 0 when input_scan_number <= 1; smoothing_ok latches -1 then. The port always used c.known, and the existing test cuts only at SOS boundaries, so it never saw this. Fix, plus a test with 7 mid-scan cuts of SUB_0 using Pillow C-path digests (the unfixed code fails 3 of them): a local patch (git apply --check clean on 86affc9). It adds Comp.prev_known, Decoder.scans and Decoder.last_good, and smooths every component with per-iMCU-row latched bits. With it, all 73,481 + 3,000 agree with the C path; the 15 left are *_hdr files whose damaged FF D8 FF signature load_image refuses before the decoder runs, as Pillow does. ftx-trace tests, both raster/trace oracles, fmt and clippy pass. If 86affc9 is pushed without it, I will push the fix on top.

The oracle's 3 retry cases are now bit-identical (they were refused), and all 69 stress traces match vectorize.py, drafts and masks (8 were refused). With the platform libm swapped in for det::, all 1,012 are, so the other 16 are item (2): limited mitre at exact reversals, whose bevel ends sit on the offset lines. Measured: macOS sin/cos are not correctly rounded on ~4% of arguments, so a correctly rounded det wouldn't match them either. Envelope digits use a correctly rounded ln (det::ln is up to 3 ulp off beside powers of ten, which changes GEOS's digit count). title: FTX-20 Photogrammetry core
description:
## Background & Vision Alignment
`FTX-20` (`COMPREHENSIVE_PLAN_FOR_THE_DESIGN_OF_FRANKENTEXTILES.md §10.2`, `docs/bundle-adjustment.md`, `docs/sheet-pose.md`, `docs/still-window.md`, `docs/triangulation.md`, `docs/video-frame-selection.md`) implements the multi-view photogrammetry core for measuring a moving child from short video clips or multi-angle photo bursts with a calibration sheet in the scene.

## Current Code State (as of 2026-10-14 Reality Check)
- **Already implemented in `crates/ftx-measure/src/`**:
  - `video/` (`select_video_frames`, `VideoFrameCandidate`, `FrameSelectionConfig`): frame identity by timestamp (`timestamp_us`), separate Tenengrad/Laplacian sharpness gates inside the person mask and on the calibration sheet, motion-blur rejection, and temporal diversity selection.
  - `sheet_pose.rs` (`estimate_sheet_pose`, `SheetPose`): planar homography decomposition (IPPE both-branch evaluation) + Levenberg-Marquardt 6-DoF camera-to-sheet pose refinement, reprojection RMS, and pose conditioning diagnostics.
  - `still_window.rs` (`find_still_windows`, `StillWindow`): detects contiguous quasi-static child pause windows across frames where inter-frame keypoint displacement is below the stillness threshold, rejecting articulated motion across views.
  - `triangulation.rs` (`triangulate_landmarks`, `TriangulatedPoint`): multi-ray SVD/DLT triangulation with Sampson/reprojection error gating, minimum inter-ray baseline angle check (refusing near-collinear rays), and anisotropic 3D covariance propagation.
  - `bundle.rs` (`adjust_bundle`, `BundleProblem`, `BundleSolution`): joint factor-graph optimization over camera poses, 3D sheet corners (metric scale anchor), and 3D body landmarks within each still window, with held-out frame partition cross-validation (`holdout_rms_mm`).
- **Remaining work to complete `FTX-20`**:
  1. **End-to-end CLI & pipeline orchestration (`FTX-20a`)**:
     - Wire `ftx measure photogrammetry --input SPEC.json [--out FILE] [--json]` in `crates/ftx-cli/src/measure.rs` chaining frame selection -> sheet pose -> still windows -> gated triangulation -> bundle adjustment with held-out partitions.
  2. **Synthetic multi-camera moving-child benchmark & refusal tests**:
     - Verify exact synthetic 3D landmark recovery (< 1.0 mm RMS on noise-free synthetic rig, calibrated uncertainty coverage under pixel noise, and refusal when baseline angle or stillness gates fail).
  3. **Truth-source update (`FTX-24a`)**:
     - Record `FTX-20` modules and test IDs in `FEATURE_PARITY.md`.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Video frame selection (timestamp identity, person/sheet sharpness, distortion), planar sheet pose (IPPE + LM), still windows, gated triangulation, and metric-scale bundle adjustment with held-out partitions pass synthetic known-answer tests
- [ ] End-to-end photogrammetry CLI subcommand wired and tested (ftx-uql)
close_reason: Completed FTX-20 photogrammetry core (video-select, still-window, camera/sheet-pose, triangulate with click-noise covariance, bundle-adjust)

title: FTX-20a End-to-end CLI wiring for photogrammetry (FTX-20) and multi-frame body fitting (FTX-21)
description:
## Background & Vision Alignment
Plan §10.2 (`Photogrammetry of a Moving Child`), Plan §9.4 (`Multi-frame Body Fit`), and Plan §14 (`CLI: ftx`) promise an end-to-end pipeline from multi-frame video/photo observations of a child moving past a metric reference sheet to a fitted Anny body (`ftx-body-fit/1`) that drives `ftx body --body-fit`, `ftx drape --body-fit`, and `ftx round WS --sim --body-fit`.

Reality Check code audit revealed a classic high-leverage integration gap:
- `crates/ftx-measure` ALREADY contains the complete photogrammetry core (`video/` frame selection, `sheet_pose.rs` IPPE planar pose + LM refinement, `still_window.rs` kinematic pause detection, `triangulation.rs` DLT + Sampson/reprojection/ray-angle gating, and `bundle.rs` sparse LM factor graph with metric scale and held-out frame partitions).
- `crates/ftx-body` ALREADY contains the complete multi-frame body fitter (`crates/ftx-body/src/multiframe.rs`, `fit_multiframe`) and `crates/ftx-cli/src/body_source.rs` ALREADY consumes `ftx-body-fit/1` reports!
- However, NEITHER `ftx-measure`'s photogrammetry pipeline NOR `ftx-body`'s `fit_multiframe` is exposed on the `ftx` CLI (`crates/ftx-cli/src/measure.rs` and `crates/ftx-cli/src/main.rs`)!

## Implementation Plan
1. **`ftx measure photogrammetry --input SPEC.json [--out FILE] [--json]` (`crates/ftx-cli/src/measure.rs`)**:
   - Accept a deterministic `ftx-photogrammetry-input/1` JSON document containing camera intrinsics/distortion, per-frame sheet corner observations, per-frame 2D person keypoints/landmarks, and optional frame candidate metadata.
   - Run `estimate_sheet_pose` per frame -> `find_still_windows` -> `triangulate_landmarks` within each still window -> `adjust_bundle` (with held-out partition cross-validation).
   - Emit a `ftx-photogrammetry/1` JSON report recording selected still windows, camera poses, 3D metric landmarks, propagated uncertainties `sigma_mm`, reprojection residuals, and held-out partition errors.
2. **`ftx body --multiframe SPEC.json --out DIR [--measurements M] [--pose drape|rest|arms-up|seated|squat] [--model PATH] [--json]` (`crates/ftx-cli/src/body_source.rs` & `main.rs`)**:
   - Accept a `ftx-multiframe-input/1` JSON document (or combined photogrammetry + tape + 2D keypoint/silhouette observations).
   - Run `ftx_body::multiframe::fit_multiframe(&model, &input)`, write `DIR/body_fit.json` (`schema: "ftx-body-fit/1"`), `DIR/body.obj`, and `DIR/body.json` (`schema: "ftx-body/1"`), including explicit ambiguity flags and residuals.
   - Ensure `DIR/body_fit.json` is directly accepted by `ftx body --body-fit DIR/body_fit.json --out NEW_DIR`, `ftx drape --body-fit DIR/body_fit.json`, and `ftx round WS --sim --body-fit DIR/body_fit.json`.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] ftx measure photogrammetry --input SPEC.json [--out FILE] [--json] runs sheet_pose -> still_window -> triangulation -> bundle and emits ftx-photogrammetry/1 JSON
- [ ] ftx body --multiframe SPEC.json --out DIR [--measurements M] [--pose POSE] [--model PATH] [--json] runs fit_multiframe and emits body_fit.json (ftx-body-fit/1), body.obj, and body.json
- [ ] End-to-end test verifies that body_fit.json produced by ftx body --multiframe is accepted by ftx body --body-fit and ftx drape --body-fit
notes: Refinement Pass: Ensure ftx body --multiframe writes body_fit.json with schema ftx-body-fit/1 matching crates/ftx-cli/src/body_source.rs so ftx body --body-fit, ftx drape --body-fit, and ftx round --body-fit consume it with zero adapter glue.
